title: Forbidden City: 9,999 Rooms? Surveys Count 8,886 | China Travel Expert
description:
You'll hear the Forbidden City has 9,999 rooms. Every real survey counts fewer.

The 9,999 (or "9,999 and a half") figure is folklore - a lucky, auspicious number tied to the emperor, not an actual count. When architectural historians survey the palace, they count about 8,886 bays across roughly 980 surviving buildings. UNESCO describes it loosely as "nearly 10,000 rooms."

The catch is the unit: Chinese halls are counted in jian (间) - the bay, the space framed by four pillars - not in "rooms" the way we picture them. So the real number depends entirely on how you define a room, which is exactly why the counts vary from survey to survey.

🧭 Expert Tip: don't try to "see every room." Walk the central axis - Meridian Gate, the three great halls, the inner court - and you've seen the building that mattered most, without chasing a number that was never real.

故宫“9999 间房”是吉祥传说，不是实数；专家按“间”（四根柱子之间的空间）清点，约 980 座现存建筑、共约 8886 间。
